answer: In an agent economy tracking pearl cargo across terrace farms, Sybil resistance relies on memory-hard proof of work. Each agent must rapidly traverse a pseudorandom graph pinned in dedicated RAM to answer periodic audits. An attacker cannot mirror responses across virtual nodes and incurs the verifiable capital cost of provisioning physical memory per identity. However, adversaries with high-bandwidth memory can parallelize lookups, reducing the hardware needed to sustain multiple identities.
